notes: Portrait, taken standing in a narrow aisle of a used bookshop: two tall wooden mystery bookcases on the left seen at a steep angle with yellow alphabet tabs, and a white romance bookcase on the right seen more straight-on. Even indoor light, no glare, in focus but the mass-market spines are small at this distance. English throughout. Titles read from spines at full resolution with three crops (left bookcase upper shelves, left bookcase middle shelves, the Nicholas Sparks and Good in Bed area on the right); labelled only what reads with confidence. Partial: A is for Alibi (Sue Grafton spine cut by the tab, 'A IS F...'), Chasing Cézanne (small type on a Peter Mayle spine), Dreaming of the Bones (Deborah Crombie spine partly hidden). Left out: several hundred spines too small or too oblique to read, in particular the whole middle bookcase except Harlan Coben's Home, the Danielle Steel and other romance shelves on the right where only author names read, the Mrs. Jeffries, Sue Grafton and Ngaio Marsh spines whose titles do not resolve, the stacks of loose paperbacks lying on shelves, and the maroon set of matching volumes at the far left. The draft's 'The Sherlockian' and 'Bleeding Hearts' could not be found; 'Bless Me a Sun' is printed 'Blaze Me a Sun' and 'Muffin Man' is 'Muffin to Fear'. Non-book items: yellow paper alphabet dividers, a handwritten 'Fiction' label. Drafted by claude-sonnet-5 (extraction 72), verified by an agent.
